Chainstay Joggle Jig

Two PPA-CF dies kink a drive-side chainstay outward: one bend out before the dimple, a straight supported run past the dimple, one bend back in after it toward the dropout. Six M8 bolts and two steel backing bars supply the force.

How it works

  1. Check the stay with the section gauges (gauges.py), then print the straight test-fit dies in cheap PLA. They should close fully on the stay with the fingers just touching its top and bottom. If not, re-measure.
  2. Remove wheel and crankset. Put both dies around the stay with their end butted against the end of the chainstay lug; that sets the position.
  3. Fill the dimple flush with steel epoxy putty, cling film between putty and stay. Scrape it level with the tube and let it cure fully. The smooth die wall then supports the dimple like the rest of the tube.
  4. Put the steel bars on both backs, insert the 6 bolts, and tighten in a cross pattern a quarter turn at a time. The tire-side bar is shorter and starts 36 mm from the lug.
  5. The die faces bottom out on each other. That is the hard stop: the cavity then equals the final (overbent) shape.
  6. Open the jig and measure the springback. Adjust OVERBEND in the script and reprint if needed. Try it on a scrap tube first.

Still to measure

  • Dimple height. The model guesses 18 mm.
  • BB centre to axle, and the rear spacing. They set the return slope and the tire numbers.
  • Whether the lug end is square or a long point. The dies butt against it.

Open points

  • BEND 1The outward bend is centred 22 mm from the lug and runs 14 mm into the putty-filled dimple. Rough force: 30–36 kN, half of a bend right at the lug, but still the hardest spot for the dies. Watch the dies there on the first test bend.
  • BOLTSThe open jig needs 74.3 mm of grip. Use M8×80.
  • CHAINRINGThe drive stay moves toward the chainring along the dimple. A 40T ring keeps about 7.4 mm, a 52T only about 2.3 mm.
  • DRILLUse a printed die as the drilling template: clamp it to the bar, mark through its bolt holes, drill 8.5 mm.
  • PRINTPrint each die on its flat back: the cavity faces up with no supports, and the clamp load compresses across the layers.
  • FRAMEOnly cold-set steel. Check dropout alignment and rear spacing afterwards, because the stay stays fixed at both ends.
  • OTHER SIDEFlip the same jig 180° around its length axis for the non-drive stay. No putty needed there.
